candidate_implies_source.reasoning: Every source-admissible execution gives a finite binary tree, its leaf values, and one bounded relative-error witness per internal addition. The candidate's computed evaluation reproduces that execution. Its contribution list contains each exact partial sum times its local error and precisely the strict-ancestor factors, so its equality yields the full selected identity.

source_implies_candidate.reasoning: The candidate represents the source's real relative-error tree model directly. Its recursive computed values obey the source's local addition equation, and its flattened sum is the same internal-node sum as equation (2.3), with reordered real summands. The singleton case reduces to zero equals the empty sum.

rationale: The candidate faithfully expresses Lemma 2.2's first explicit forward-error identity. It retains arbitrary binary tree shapes, arbitrary signed real inputs, exact partial sums, and computed-child operands linked to local rounding witnesses. The flattened contribution list includes every internal node once and accumulates only strict-ancestor factors. It adds no successful-run or existence restriction and retains all higher-order products.
